_README: Frozen authentication shape of every registered route. Generated by
This is a record of what each route LOOKED LIKE when it was last
reviewed. It is not a statement that these routes are safe. An entry
reading 'unknown' is not an accusation and an entry reading 'user' is
not a guarantee -- see the docstring of services/route_auth.py.
If a test fails against this file, the question to ask is 'did my
change remove a gate?', not 'how do I regenerate this?'.

pulse_web_app_shell.evidence: declared:public (Static shell only -- an empty <div id="root"> plus one hashed script and one hashed stylesheet. It carries no member data, so there is nothing here for a gate to protect. Gating it would be actively wrong: the server would redirect to the legacy login before the client could boot and route to its own login screen, losing the destination URL. Every /api/ call the shell goes on to make is authenticated independently -- that is where the member data actually crosses the wire, and that is where the gates are.)
